approved: Sharon Claydon The question is that the amendment be agreed to.

Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill and Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill (No. 1) stand referred to the Federation Chamber after adjournment of debate on their second-reading motions.

Argued that the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2026 makes useful but modest administrative changes, including intellectual property, antidumping and "tell us once" reforms, while raising concerns about reduced advertising-spending transparency and notification of adverse allegations. Said the coalition will not oppose it in the House but will seek a Senate inquiry.

Supported the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2026, which contains 21 measures amending 26 acts and repealing two. Said it would reduce compliance burdens, update intellectual property and customs rules, simplify gender-equality reporting and government-service processes, and improve administrative efficiency; later raised concerns about removing some advertising disclosures before commending the bill to the House.

Supported the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2026 while moving an amendment seeking measurable regulatory reduction targets, senior accountability, faster decisions, stronger impact assessment and greater funding for the National Productivity Fund; in summing up, the government said its agenda would reduce regulatory burden by $10.2 billion annually, amend 25 acts and improve 18 agencies, but the amendment question remained unresolved.
